_note: Town-specific resale facts. Each fact was read on an official municipal web page, municipal code (eCode360 / General Code) or official municipal form on the 'checked' date. status: verified = resale requirement + issuing office confirmed from an official source; partial = some facts confirmed, others still need a call to the municipality. Anything not listed here is shown as 'Not yet verified'.

linwood-city.requirement: Resale certificate of occupancy (resale inspection) required before sale
linwood-city.issuer: City of Linwood: Construction Official or designee (resale inspections scheduled through Fire Prevention / Housing, 609-926-7953)
linwood-city.fee: Not published for resales (the Chapter 212 fees listed are for rental registration only). Ask the city.
details: City Code §212-9: no one may "sell, rent, transfer ... of any dwelling unit" unless a certificate of occupancy certifying it is fit for habitation and complies with city ordinances has been issued by the Construction Official or designee, upon inspection.
City construction page: "Resale Inspections (residential) Monday thru Friday by appointment", contact 609-926-7953.
The state smoke-alarm/CO requirements still apply. Under the state rule, when a town has its own inspection, the town checks smoke and CO alarms before issuing its certificate.

sources.label: City of Linwood: Construction & Zoning page

absecon-city.requirement: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) required on any change of owner, tenant or occupant
absecon-city.issuer: City of Absecon Code Enforcement (Construction Office), (609) 641-0663 ext. 113
absecon-city.fee: $35 per single-family residence (CCO application, includes 1 inspection + 1 reinspection; $25 per additional reinspection), per Code Ch. 160. Note: the construction fee schedule in the same chapter separately lists $111 for a 'certificate of continued occupancy'. Confirm which applies.
details: City page: "Chapter 160 of the Code of Absecon requires all properties having a change in owner, tenant or occupant receive a certificate of continuing occupancy" (property maintenance compliance); residential properties must also meet N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 smoke/CO rules.

atlantic-city.requirement: Occupancy permit required before the sale of residential property involving a new occupancy
atlantic-city.issuer: City of Atlantic City (Licensing & Inspection / Code Enforcement)
atlantic-city.fee: $75 per residential building, or $75 per unit in buildings with 2+ units; $50 per unit per reinspection (Code §194-4, amended 2023)
details: Code §194-1B: "The owner of any residential property shall obtain an occupancy permit prior to the sale of such property involving a new occupancy"; not required for sale of vacant properties until a new occupancy occurs.

sources.label: Atlantic City Code Ch. 194 Occupancy Permits, eCode360

galloway-township.requirement: Fire certificate only (smoke alarms, CO alarms, extinguisher). No separate resale CO in the code section reviewed.
galloway-township.fee: $45 if requested >10 business days before change of ownership; $90 at 4–10 days; $161 at <4 days (Code §153-11.1)
details: Code §153-11.1: "Upon the change of ownership (resale) of any real property a fire certificate must be applied for, for the inspection of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers only." Must be done before the new owners occupy. (Note: state law dropped the extinguisher requirement in 2025; see the smoke/CO page.)
Separate certificates of occupancy apply to rentals and commercial rentals (§153-11.2, §153-11.2A).

sources.label: Galloway Code Ch. 153, Fire Certificates and Certificates of Occupancy, eCode360

egg-harbor-township.requirement: Smoke/CO certificate required (Fire Inspections). The township CCO form lists a 'CCO Residential Changes' fee. Confirm whether a CCO applies to your resale.
egg-harbor-township.issuer: Egg Harbor Township Fire Inspections (Planning & Development)
egg-harbor-township.fee: Smoke detector application: $54 (township page). CCO form: 'CCO Residential Changes: $200'.
details: Township page: "The fee for the Smoke Detector Application is $54.00" (Certification of Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance).
The Continued Certificate of Occupancy application (2024 form) lists residential and commercial change fees of $200. It does not say whether every residential resale needs a CCO.

brigantine-city.requirement: Smoke/CO/extinguisher compliance certificate required before settlement. No general resale CO confirmed.
brigantine-city.fee: The city fee schedule (Code Art. II) lists two entries for this certificate: $45 / $90 / $161, and $35 / $70 / $125 (≥11, 4–10 and <4 business days before settlement). Confirm the current amount with the city.
details: Both entries appear in the City of Brigantine Fees Schedule on eCode360. Ask Fire Prevention which one applies.

buena-vista-township.requirement: Resale smoke/CO certificate from the township Fire Prevention Bureau. No separate resale CO found.
buena-vista-township.issuer: Buena Vista Township Fire Prevention Bureau, 890 Harding Highway; (856) 697-2100
buena-vista-township.fee: See the township's resale/rental smoke inspection instructions (payment schedule in the PDF)
details: The Fire Prevention page offers 'Resale / Rental Smoke Inspections and Instructions' and a 'Resale / Rental Smoke Certification Application', and says not to use the state DFS link for resale applications.

sources.label: Buena Vista Twp Fire Prevention Bureau

buena-borough.requirement: The borough site lists a 'Resale Inspection for Properties' service. The state Division of Fire Safety handles smoke detector certifications.
buena-borough.issuer: Buena Borough Construction Code office (616 Central Ave, Minotola; 856-697-9393) for resale inspection; NJ Division of Fire Safety for the smoke certificate
buena-borough.fee: Not published on the pages reviewed
details: Borough Construction page: "State of NJ Division of Fire Safety covers ... Smoke Detector Certifications."

hamilton-township.requirement: Smoke/CO certificate inspection by the Fire Prevention Bureau before resale/reoccupancy. No resale CO found.
hamilton-township.issuer: Hamilton Township (Atlantic) Fire Prevention Bureau; schedule via the Construction Office
hamilton-township.fee: $50 standard (within 10 business days); $135 rush (within 3 business days); one free reinspection (township application, Code Ch. 170)
details: Construction page: inspectors "inspect smoke and carbon monoxide detectors prior to the resale/reoccupancy of residences".

hammonton-town.requirement: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) and inspection required whenever a property is sold. Apply at least 30 days before closing.
hammonton-town.issuer: Town of Hammonton Construction Department, 100 Central Ave; 609-567-4300 ext. 108
hammonton-town.fee: Not published. The town says to contact it for CCO fees.
details: "Whenever a property is sold, rented, leased commercially, or transferred, it is necessary to apply for a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)" (residential rentals now use Rental Registration instead).
A residential smoke & CO certification application is posted on the same page.

longport-borough.requirement: Land Use Compliance / Certificate of Occupancy inspection for sale, plus a separate smoke detector compliance certificate
longport-borough.issuer: Longport Building & Zoning Dept (2305 Atlantic Ave; 609-823-2731) plus Longport Bureau of Fire Prevention (609-822-9578)
longport-borough.fee: $150 land use application + $75 smoke certificate ($30 per reinspection)
details: Application asks for a current survey, flood elevation certificate and the sales contract (Ordinance §70-2).

sources.label: Longport Application for Land Use Compliance of a Property for Sale (PDF)

margate-city.requirement: Land Use Certificate application (title transfers) must be completed before closing
margate-city.fee: The 2025 city fee schedule lists 'Certificate of Continued Occupancy: $168'. Confirm the Land Use Certificate fee with the city.
details: City page: "To purchase or sell a property, a Land Use Certificate application must be completed before closing."

northfield-city.requirement: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (resale) inspection, including smoke and CO alarms and heating certification
northfield-city.fee: $65 non-refundable; $25 per reinspection; possible extra $10 if settlement is 5 days or less away
details: The packet requires a heating certification for oil/gas units from an NJ-licensed plumber or HVAC contractor.

somers-point-city.issuer: City of Somers Point (Construction, Zoning & Code Enforcement)
somers-point-city.fee: $250 per residential resale inspection (fee schedule in Jan. 23, 2025 council minutes); lead-based paint inspection $50

sources.label: Somers Point council minutes, Jan 23 2025: fee schedule (PDF)

ventnor-city.requirement: Land Use form and Sale Certificate of Occupancy (per unit) required to sell
details: FAQ: "In order to sell your home you will need a Land Use and Sale Certificate of Occupancy (per unit). Each form is $50.00."

weymouth-township.requirement: Township Certificate of Occupancy for sale, plus the state DCA Division of Fire Safety smoke/CO certificate
weymouth-township.issuer: Weymouth Township Housing Officer (609-476-2633); smoke/CO certificate from NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety
weymouth-township.fee: $50 township CO inspection fee; state DFS fee is separate
details: Form: "A Certificate of Occupancy will not be issued until Weymouth Township receives a valid New Jersey DCA, Division of Fire Safety (DFS) Certificate ..."

sources.label: Weymouth Application for Certificate of Occupancy (Aug 2026 form, PDF)

mullica-township.requirement: The township forms page lists a 'Resale Application' under Code Enforcement, Zoning & Housing
mullica-township.fee: Not confirmed (the application PDF could not be read)

pleasantville-city.requirement: The city posts a 2025 smoke/CO/extinguisher certification application. A continued Permit of Occupancy is described for existing buildings/offices; residential resale applicability not confirmed.

ocean-city.requirement: Smoke detector & CO alarm compliance certificate before sale (in-person inspection). Homes built after Jan 1, 1996 also need Zoning Compliance Certification.
ocean-city.issuer: City of Ocean City (Fire Prevention / Knight Building)
ocean-city.fee: $50 per unit (built before 1996) or $100 per unit (built after 1996), per the 2025 sale application
details: Applies to units in 1–2 family dwellings and individually owned condo units in multifamily buildings.

sources.label: Ocean City Inspection Request: Sale of Property, 2025 (PDF)
Ocean City Code Ch. 30 Municipal Fees, eCode360

stone-harbor-borough.requirement: Certificate of Title Transfer (zoning inspection) required before transfer of title, plus a smoke/CO certificate from the Fire Prevention Bureau
stone-harbor-borough.issuer: Stone Harbor Zoning Officer (title transfer) and Stone Harbor Fire Prevention Bureau
stone-harbor-borough.fee: Fire Bureau certificate: $50 for 1 unit if requested >10 business days ahead (more for multiple units or short notice; 2021 form). Title transfer fee per Code §214-6 / borough application.
details: Code §214-3: required on every resale, even within 18 months of new construction; §214-5: the Zoning Officer inspects for zoning compliance.

sources.label: Stone Harbor Code Ch. 214 Certificate of Title Transfer, eCode360
Application for Certificate of Title Transfer (PDF)

wildwood-city.requirement: Combined Transfer of Ownership application: Continued Occupancy (CCO), smoke/CO certificate, zoning certification and (except single-family) status of fire code
wildwood-city.issuer: City of Wildwood (Construction Office / Fire Department)
wildwood-city.fee: CCO $95 (1–5 units); smoke/CO $45 / $90 / $161 per unit (≥10, 4–10, <4 business days); zoning cert $50 / $70 / $125; status of fire code $25

sources.label: City of Wildwood Application for Transfer of Ownership (PDF)

north-wildwood-city.requirement: Forms required for sale include a Certificate of Zoning Use Compliance and a separate fire (smoke/CO) certificate
north-wildwood-city.issuer: North Wildwood Planning & Zoning; Fire Prevention & Inspection Bureau
north-wildwood-city.fee: Zoning certificate: $50 (>10 business days), $70 (4–9 days), $125 (<4 days); fire certificate billed separately
details: "SEPARATE CHECKS (if applicable) ARE REQUIRED FOR FIRE & ZONING CERTIFICATES"; 2.75% card surcharge.

sources.label: North Wildwood Forms required for sale of properties (PDF, 2026)

wildwood-crest-borough.requirement: Smoke/CO certificate (CSACMAPFEC) from the Fire Prevention Bureau before closing. Other resale certificates not confirmed.
wildwood-crest-borough.fee: $50 (>10 business days), $90 (4–10), $160 (<4); $50 reinspection; $1,000 penalty if not obtained before closing (2026 application)

cape-may-city.requirement: Fire Prevention Bureau inspection for sales of 1–2 family homes. The bureau notes extinguishers are no longer required for 1–2 family sales or rentals.
cape-may-city.issuer: City of Cape May Bureau of Fire Prevention, 712 Washington St; 609-884-9599
cape-may-city.fee: Not confirmed (the city's Sale of Property form could not be loaded)
details: Bureau page: "Fire Extinguishers are no longer required in One- or Two Family Dwellings (For Sales and/or Rentals)."

sources.label: Cape May City Fire Prevention Bureau

avalon-borough.requirement: Smoke & CO inspection requested through the borough (online form linked from the Fire Prevention page). Other resale certificates not confirmed.
avalon-borough.issuer: Borough of Avalon Fire Prevention / Licensing; (609) 967-5918 to schedule

lower-township.requirement: The Fire Bureau posts a '2026 Residential Application for Sales and Rentals'. Resale CO not confirmed.
lower-township.issuer: Lower Township Bureau of Fire Safety

middle-township.requirement: Smoke/CO certificate. Middle Township is served by more than one fire district (the DCA portal lists districts 001–004), so the issuing bureau depends on the property's district.
middle-township.issuer: For Fire Districts #1, 3 & 4: Bureau of Fire Prevention, 115 Mechanic St, Cape May Court House; 609-465-8710
middle-township.fee: Districts 1/3/4 (2025 packet): $78 (>10 days), $115 (4–10 days), $210 (<4 days); $75 reinspection
details: The certificate is issued to the seller; open construction permits block issuance (2025 packet).

upper-township.requirement: Fire certificate only. The township does not do resale inspections; the smoke/CO certificate is administered by NJ DCA.
upper-township.issuer: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety (apply via the DCA Fire Safety portal)
upper-township.fee: State fee schedule (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9): $45 / $90 / $161 depending on notice
details: Township page: "The Construction Department does not do inspections for resale of residential or non-residential structures ... This certification is administered by the NJ Department of Community Affairs."

sources.label: NJ DCA Fire Safety portal: smoke certification

dennis-township.requirement: Fire safety inspection (smoke/CO) required on sale before transfer. No resale CO found.
dennis-township.issuer: Dennis Township Fire Prevention / Bureau of Fire Safety, 571 Petersburg Rd, Dennisville
dennis-township.fee: $100 (>10 business days), $150 (4–10 days), $200 (≤4 days); $500–$2,000 penalty if transferred uninspected

sources.label: Dennis Twp Fire Safety Inspection Application for sale of property (PDF, 2025)

cape-may-point-borough.requirement: Certificate of Land Use Compliance required before selling or transferring title (exception: new construction with a CO issued within 18 months)
cape-may-point-borough.issuer: Borough of Cape May Point (zoning inspection)
details: The issuer of the smoke/CO certificate was not confirmed.

sources.label: Cape May Point Code Ch. 67 Certificate of Land Use Compliance, eCode360

west-wildwood-borough.requirement: The borough forms page lists 'Smoke Detector CO2 alarm Compliance certification'. Resale CO not confirmed.
